score.note: Improved from differing_halfwords=3 by eliminating the separate `s32 error` local entirely and writing `result = 0 - 9` / `result = 0 - 3` directly at each site (the goto-target `negate:` label is now a no-op). The second occurrence (result = 0 - 3) now compiles byte-identical to the reference (movs r7,#3 / negs r7,r7), confirming the hypothesis: the reference reuses r7 -- already dead from the early `result = 0` -- for the error/negate computation, and the separate `error` local was blocking that reuse. One residual remains at the FIRST occurrence (result = 0 - 9): r7 is provably 0 on that control-flow path, so this compiler folds the whole computation into a single `subs r7, #9`, where the reference instead materializes `movs r7, #9` and jumps forward to share the second occurrence's `negs r7, r7`. Two attempts to force a real shared negate (goto negate; ... negate: result = -result / result = 0 - result, applied symmetrically) each regressed sharply (wrong length, wrong_instructions >=36) rather than converging -- this compiler will not give up the subs-fold once r7's liveness is transparent enough to prove it. Needs the same class of fix as the allocator-order/liveness lever being built for the wider register-wall cluster, not another manual respelling of this pair.

decoder_evidence: The structurally correct shared-negate s32 form raises result pseudo 34 from 5 uses, 4 sets, span 82 to 7 uses, 5 sets, span 86.
That moves result ahead of the save-slot address in lreg priority, so result takes r6 and the address is forced to r7.
The separate-magnitude form preserves address=r6 and result=r7, but combine replaces magnitude-to-result copy plus negate with a cross-register negate, reusing r6 for the path-disjoint magnitude.
